title: Sigmoid compute curves, plasticity loss, and ReDo resets
brief: Fit ScaleRL's sigmoidal compute-performance curve and see when its asymptote can't be trusted, then watch a small network lose its ability to fit new targets and get it back with resets.
hints: Rearrange the sigmoid for a fixed A: (A - R0) / (R - R0) - 1 = (C_mid / C)^B, so its log is B log C_mid - B log C, a straight line in log C.
np.linalg.lstsq with columns [1, log C] returns (intercept, slope). B is minus the slope, and C_mid is exp(intercept / B).
For effective_rank, np.linalg.svd(features, compute_uv=False) returns the singular values in decreasing order. np.searchsorted on their normalised cumulative sum finds k.
A unit is dead on x when h.max(axis=0) <= 0 for its column. Record which units are dead in both layers before you change any weights.
In redo_reset, zero the dead unit's column in the next layer, net[2].weight[:, dead] or net[4].weight[:, dead], so the network's outputs don't change.
Take x and every y from one torch.Generator, in the order the docstring gives, so your run matches the checks.
